posts.title: This is now officially the longest Cop
posts.text: By the way, the conference has now tipped over to win the dubious honour of becoming the longest Cop ever. That crown was previously worn by Cop25 in Madrid, in 2019, which overran by 44 hours overtime, and was gavelled to a close at 13.55pm, CET. This one is still going with the end absolutely nowhere in sight.

A dramatic intervention now from the Ireland climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, who says on behalf of the EU, they can not accept the Antalya Pact in its current form. This is very significant. Even though the minister was speaking about an agenda item that had not even been called yet, this shows clearly that the…

posts.title: The EU has now formally objected to the final deal
posts.text: The EU has now formally objected to the final with Darragh O’Brien telling the plenary: “We want to formally object to the Antalya pact because it fails to meet the moment. We express profound disappointent with the cover decision at a point when the world urgently needs action. “We will not endorse a decision that…

The Swiss delegation has asked the presidency to make sure they allow countries time to speak before decisions get gavelled through, reflecting some disquiet among some about the speed with which the Turkish presidency is proceeding.

If the main decision is adopted it is going to be called the “Antalya Pact”. Did I say if? Subtle changes have been made to the new draft decision, such as changing the term ’accelerating’ to ‘increasing’ in the context of Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage. But fossil fuels have still not made the text.

posts.title: As the closing plenary begins what are the options?
posts.text: The latest draft text is out, the ministers are in plenary, some have been in “huddles” and now the plenary is beginning. What are the options from here? One is that there is no agreement in this room and the talks will collapse. Another is that there is agreement and the text will be accepted. The third is that…

The Cop president Murat Kurum has now opened the closing plenary and is addressing the summit. He starts by saying the room is “on the verge” of a historic decision. He thanks his Australian “friends” and Chris Bowen and his team. He is thanking lots of other people too. He says: “No one got everything they wanted but…

Moments before the plenary started the new text was put out by the Presidency. According to the UN press office, the changes from the previous text include: Recalling of some of the key decisions made since the adoption of the Paris Agreement Changing the term ’accelerating’ to ‘increasing’ in the context of Carbon…

I am inside the plenary now and there is a huddle on stage that includes Chris Bowen, Murat Kurum and Simon Stiell. They look animated but not happy. Lots of people are staring intently to try and interpret what’s going on. I have to say that Bowen looks quite despondent. He has some of Australia’s very experienced…

COP31 is diminishing “by the hour,” Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said Sunday as the climate talks pushed deep into extra time, according to AFP. A proposed agreement “lacks the climate ambition that is needed to tackle this climate crisis. We’re very disappointed by that,” said O’Brien, whose…

The UN climate chief, Simon Stiell, has just walked into the plenary room. I know it’s dangerous to interpret how someone is feeling by how they look. But we will give it a go. Unhappy. The Australian climate change minister, Chris Bowen, the president of negotiations, is up at the stage. He was asked if the talks…

posts.title: Germany says it will reject the current text
posts.text: My colleague Graham Readfearn has just been listening to a press conference from the German delegation. He says that the German climate minister, Carsten Schneider, has stated he will reject the current text of the agreement in Antalya. He was speaking in German, but according to a native German speaker next to…

Mohamed Adow, director of Power Shift Africa, has been looking through the text and says: “This latest text is a total mess and countries should throw it out. It fails to deliver vital climate finance to the vulnerable while promoting far-fetched and eye wateringly expensive carbon removal technologies which is a gift…

A Turkish journalist colleague, Selin Ugurtas, who writes for the climate news agency Iklim Masasi, has told me a little more of Kurum’s statement just now. She says he said: “If there is no agreement on the decision, [parties blocking] should consider that they would be blocking the Cop process and evaluate…

posts.title: Miliband says current food exports red tape 'worst of both worlds'
posts.text: The Tories and Reform have made the argument this morning that the new food deal is “bad” for British farmers, because they will be subject to EU rules and standards. They say more than 90% of British farmers currently don’t export to the EU- so why should Britain have to cede that control over standards? The…

Reform UK’s deputy leader Richard Tice has also slammed the new EU agreements as “a really bad deal”. He says “it’s not a reset, it’s a reverse” and claims that it won’t add to GDP but actually reduce GDP. The government says it could lead to a 0.5% bump. Tice doesn’t elaborate on details here, or where that cost will…

posts.title: Tories would repeal new EU deals on food, trade, youth visas
posts.text: A chief concern for the Europeans as to the idea of the UK rejoining the bloc is frankly, the lack of British political stability this past decade, and the fear that a change in government down the line would lead to another backflip. Burghart this morning went as far as saying that a future Tory government would…

Foreign secretary Ed Miliband on the BBC was also pressed on the business argument that cutting EU red tape on food and agricultural trade will make a grocery shop cheaper. Kuennsberg raises the statement from the British Retail Consortium which says that the deals to cut red tape on food and agricultural products…

Tory deputy head Alex Burghart has been arguing against the deals on Sky and the BBC this morning. He argues the removal of red tape on food and agricultural products is “really bad for business” as British farmers now will have to follow EU regulations when some don’t even trade with the bloc. He says this is a “a…

Theresa May spent three years as prime minister (2016-2019) trying to negotiate the Brexit deal, before resigning. She has told the BBC this morning she is “aghast” at the idea of Burnham resurrecting the issue, warning him of the enormous effort ahead: What I saw was that the extent of those negotiations, the hours…

Andy Burnham says these are the first steps…

posts.title: Day 13 of Cop31 – recapped
posts.text: That’s all for today – we hope everyone following from Antalya gets a good night’s sleep. Here are the highlights from the 13th day of the 31st UN climate summit, which is still not over: Activists told the Presidency this summit could be one of the ‘most disappointing Cops’ ever Carbon removal must ‘be additional,…

“Today we have listened to you and sought to find common ground for your expectations,” said Murat Kurum, thanking the tired delegates for their “constructive approach”. He said the third and final version of the cover decision will be “in your hands shortly”, and parties will have until 6am local time to consider the…

Cop31 President, Murat Kurum, has arrived on the main stage, and has been immediately swarmed by delegates. The Turkish-Australian joint presidency has kept a low public profile today, on the first day of overtime, and the transparency they promised has been somewhat hard to come by for observers of the process.…
A handful of less controversial topics have indeed gone through without issue, and the session is taking a brief break before the Cop31 President arrives.

A dispute has broken about gender – and how it is defined – with interventions from Argentina and Paraguay. The draft document “encourages” a finance committee to enhance efforts to ensure gender-responsiveness in implementing its workplan, and requests Parties to consider gender balance and geographical…

Next up is a text on long-term climate finance, which has been rejected by the African Group. “This process did not provide sufficient space for negotiations,” said the negotiator for Ghana, speaking on the group’s behalf. “For now, it is not ready on our side for adoption.” The objection is to paragraph 3, which…

The plenary session has now actually begun, and we understood that it’s only the uncontroversial topics that are to be gaveled through. However, the very first topic, on climate empowerment – helping all members of society engage in climate action – has been met with an immediate objection from Russia that has drawn…

The Guardian has been leaked a submission that the countries calling themselves the “progressive coalition” – including the EU, UK and island and developing countries – want added to the cover text that is expected to be brought to a plenary at some point in the hours ahead. It is an eleventh-hour bid to bolster the…

The plenary has been pushed back by half an hour, into Sunday morning local time. Many diplomats have gone home, eager to get some rest before the (assumed) progress at the morning plenary session. Others are taking rest where they can find it.
The plenary session has just begun. A few weary-looking delegates have started to file in but the main stage has not yet been occupied …

Neither of these things are necessarily anything to brag about, but is Cop31 about to go down as both the biggest and the longest Cop in history? It is just after 11pm here in Antalya and we have been told that a plenary will commence at 11:30pm but that this will only deal with procedural issues. We are also getting…

Why does it matter if the Cop31 deal neglects to mention fossil fuels? Here’s a quick recap. The main purpose of these annual UN climate summits is to stop the planet from heating. When world leaders signed the Paris agreement at a Cop in 2015, they bound their countries to keeping global heating by the end of the…

Three of the world’s biggest carbon polluters agreed to boost oil production this week, during talks in China that appear to have been far more fruitful than the climate summit is shaping up to be. The fuel deal between the US, China and Russia was struck on Thursday in Shenzhen, China, just as diplomats attending…

A predicament “that never should have deteriorated so far” is how Jasper Inventor, head of the Greenpeace’s delegation, has described the current situation at Cop31, as weary delegates bemoan the lack of a new draft deal or clarity over the next steps. “The fact that no text has been distributed and no actual…
